chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad al-Ash'ari, from Abdullah ibn Aamir, from Ali ibn Mahziyar, from Fazalat ibn Ayoub and Hammad ibn Isa, from Muawiya ibn Wahb, who said:
I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the most superior of the timings for Al-Witr. So he (peace be upon him) said: 'The dawn is the beginning of that'.

key_terms.أَفْضَلِ: Most superior/preferred, indicating a recommended (mustahabb) rather than obligatory status
key_terms.الْفَجْر: Dawn, the time of the Fajr prayer, marking the start of the optimal period here
key_terms.الْوَتْر: Witr, an optional night prayer performed in odd numbers of units

ai.seo_question: What is the best time to perform the Witr prayer according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi identifies dawn (Fajr) as the most virtuous time to conclude the night's optional prayers (Witr), a ruling emphasized by Imam al-Sadiq (AS). It highlights the spiritual significance of the pre-dawn hours in Shia jurisprudence, linking the completion of night worship with the onset of the Fajr prayer time. This establishes a clear preference for performing Witr immediately before or at the beginning of Fajr rather than delaying it until after sunrise.
